neighbours.label: the Pilgrims of the Mayflower: the Pilgrims, the Mayflower and its Compact, and the Plymouth colony they founded in 1620 (with or without the year); other pilgrims (religious walkers), other colonies such as Jamestown, and Thanksgiving food stay low
fire: William Bradford governed the Pilgrims at Plymouth for many years.
About a hundred passengers crowded onto the Mayflower for the crossing.
Half of the Pilgrims died during their first winter in New England.
Squanto taught the Pilgrims how to plant corn.
Before going ashore, the Mayflower's passengers signed an agreement to govern themselves.
Many Americans trace their family back to the Pilgrims who sailed in 1620.
The Pilgrims had first fled England for the Dutch city of Leiden.
A full-size replica of the Mayflower is moored in Plymouth harbour.
quiet: John Smith governed the settlers at Jamestown for a short time.
About a hundred passengers crowded onto the ferry for the crossing.
Half of the pilgrims on the Camino walk it during the summer months.
Pocahontas married the tobacco planter John Rolfe.
Before going ashore, the cruise ship's passengers signed up for a bus tour.
Many Americans trace their family back to immigrants who arrived at Ellis Island.
The Huguenots had first fled France for the Dutch city of Leiden.
